evidence.quote: Ok actual when actual = dataVersion -> ... | Ok _ -> Error "The books in this file do not match its data version."
| Some books when holdsRecords books -> { model with Error = Some "Books can only be imported into new books; ..."

ARC-REV-01.rationale: All new rules are in Tier 2: file validity, version, snapshot checks and data-version match in Summa.Storage.Transfer, and the GitHub refusal, new-books-only rule and download/import decisions in the Summa.Web.Engine update function. Tier 3 only adds three event-name to message mappings, with no predicate.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Transfer.export and read are pure and take the time as an argument. The engine uses ctx.Now for the export time and the file name's business date, and it requests the download as an OfferDownload effect and the save through the existing `save`. No clock, I/O or console use appears below Tier 4, and nothing in Tier 3 or 4 re-enters Tier 2 decisions.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The timestamp format is written as a literal in both the writer and the reader. The two copies agree, but nothing ties them together. Other facts have one definition: Schema and Version are literals that are referenced, githubTransferError is a single constant, and the classification comes from Exports.Classification. The existing download-error sentence is repeated as a literal in the engine.

evidence.quote: let contentsOf (r: Receivables) : Contents = { Customers = r.Books.Customers.Count; ...

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The counting rule and the contents-versus-books check are in Tier 2 (Transfer). The preview is built in the Tier 2 engine from Transfer.read and Transfer.contentsOf. The HTML only binds the view value.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds pure functions (contentsOf, declaredContents, transferPreview) that take no clock or I/O. The preview is a pure projection of the model's pasted text, and no new effect is introduced.

evidence.quote: when v <> 1m && v <> decimal Version -> Error $"Transfer files of version {v} cannot be read here."
when actual = dataVersion && v = 2m && not (declaredContents file = Some(contentsOf restored.Books))
| Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one definition (contentsOf), used by export, read and the preview. The version number is restated as the literals 1m and 2m beside the Version literal. The contents check is tied to 2m rather than to Version, so a later version bump would silently skip it. The copies agree today. The "This file cannot be imported: " prefix is also written both in transferPreview and in the BooksTransferImported branch, with the same text.
